result.title: TIVS: Mapping the Sensitivity Landscape of Visual Token Transformations in MLLMs
result.summary: Recent efforts to improve the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have explored visual token pruning, quantization, and feature compression. However, the properties that determine whether transformed visual tokens remain usable by a frozen decoder are not well characterized. We introduce \textbf{TIVS (Token Identity Versus Statistics)}, a training-free intervention framework that separately studies sequence permutation, token retention, numerical precision, and statistical replacement under controlled conditions. On 192 POPE questions, three token permutations change TinyLLaVA accuracy by only $-0.17$ percentage points on average, while changing 4.69\% of individual predictions. Diagonal and rank-64 Gaussian replacements decrease accuracy by 25.0 and 28.1 points on the same subset. Further experiments with exact moment constraints, quantization error, token retention, and additional visual tasks reveal how strongly the effects depend on the original feature values and the evaluation setting. These findings provide an empirical basis for assessing visual token transformations in frozen MLLMs and designing more reliable multimodal interfaces.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练干预框架 TIVS，在冻结 MLLM 上分别施加序列置换、token 保留、数值精度与统计量替换，并在 192 道 POPE 题上量化准确率与个体预测的变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断下游利用的是视觉 token 的身份还是统计量（置换仅降 0.17 点却改变 4.69% 预测），与 LVR 关注的视觉细节保留、视觉旁路和信息坍缩诊断紧密相关；但样本量小、模型单一，其敏感性景观能否外推待核查。
